title: Edward Wotton (Scotland) to Walsingham, drafts of 25 Aug, 30 Aug and 1 Sep 1585 (DECODE R4841-R4843)

steps.what: Fetched the twelve DECODE images of R4841-R4843 with the stored cookie.
Recognised the pages as Wotton's own clear-English drafts headed 'To Mr Secretary', with code numbers only for names; no letter cipher.
Identified the code numbers from context: 19 Arran, 39 Master of Gray, 10 King James (certain); 9 Elizabeth/England, 20 Maxwell, 24 Huntly, 3 France (probable).
Tried to check CSP Scotland vol. 8 for the calendared despatches and their resolved names; BHO paywalled, archive.org copy lending-only.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): the name-code table copied verbatim from NOTES.md to texts/key.md and a summary given for each draft. Missing: the three drafts (clear English with name numbers) were never transcribed into the folder, so no transcription or glossed text exists

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): each of R4841-R4843 checked: the repository holds only summaries and texts/key.md; the images (main checkout decode/) show clear drafts not transcribed. All three relabelled decoded, not read; class read -> not read; method key from adjacent plaintext -> not solved; fraction_read unknown -> 0.

Re-fetched DECODE records R4841-R4843 with the project cookie (research/reading_audit/b16_wotton_fetch.py): each still holds only its four page images, no transcription, decryption, key or attachment.

Tried CSP Scotland viii (1914) again for a text to align with: HathiTrust ssd view behind a Cloudflare check, archive.org calendarofstatep0008vari download refused (401, lending-only), the other archive.org Boyd items are earlier volumes. Nothing printed was aligned; the drafts are the primary text.

Transcribed the three drafts in full from the twelve full-resolution images, in strips and zooms (texts/R4841-R4843_transcription.txt), marking struck words, interlineations and doubtful readings; Wotton's working notes at the head of f. 167r included.

Built a reading of each draft in its last state with the name code glossed in place (texts/R484x_reading.md) and a modern-English rendering (R484x_en.md); aligned word by word with the transcription (b16_wotton_align.py): every reading word is carried or is a modernised spelling; supplied words bracketed.

Code 3 = the Queen of England, not France: 'divert 10 from 3 ... or if the King constantly in affection towards 3, convey him into France' (R4841) and 'it can no way stand with 3 honor that I should be at that time in this country' (R4843). Sense only, four occurrences, flagged for review in texts/key.md; 9 = England ('the 9 friendship') likewise sense only.

Scored the reading bodies with _check_reading.py (header cut): R4841 0.98 (51/52 sentences), R4842 0.89 (58/65), R4843 0.91 (53/58). All three relabelled read; class not read -> read; method -> key recovered based on adjacent plaintext (the name code identified from the clear text, as before the audit); fraction_read 0 -> 1.0.

v6 spelling check (23 Oct 2026, research/reading_audit/v6_spelling_files.txt): the modernised spelling of 22 Oct restored to Wotton's, word by word from his own drafts as transcribed (texts/R484x_transcription.txt, struck words dropped, interlined taken in; v6_align.py), abbreviations written out; holes and brackets kept, no word changed. Rescored with research/reading_audit/v2_score.py: texts/R4841_reading.md plain 0.962 -> 0.615, explicit holes 0.981 -> 0.981; texts/R4842_reading.md plain 0.846 -> 0.446, explicit holes 0.954 -> 0.954; texts/R4843_reading.md plain 0.877 -> 0.579, explicit holes 0.947 -> 0.947. The plain share falls with period spelling against a modern word list; the explicit-hole share, the bar for period spelling, is unchanged or the change comes from the new header lines in files without a '## Reading' heading. No state changes.

validation.notes: clear drafts with a few name-code numbers; no ciphertext transcription in the folder

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The three drafts are in clear English with a small numeric name code; the code numbers were identified from the clear text (19 Arran, 39 Master of Gray, 10 King James, 3 the Queen, 20 Maxwell) and checked where possible against CSP Scotland viii's glosses (found after the reading). The drafts were transcribed in full and read on 22 Oct 2026 (batch b16); 27, 32, 36 and 11 stay open.
outcome.notes: Drafts read in full; 7 of 11 code numbers identified (3 certain, 4 probable), 27, 32, 36, 40 open. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: no draft is transcribed here; all three decoded, not read; class read -> not read, method -> not solved. The code identifications stand. 22 Oct 2026, re-read (b16): the three drafts transcribed in full from the DECODE images and read (clean-sentence share 0.98, 0.89, 0.91); class -> read, method -> key recovered based on adjacent plaintext. Open: codes 27, 32, 36, 11 (no key material; CSP viii not reachable), a few illegible interlineations.

credits.note: CSP Scotland viii glosses fixed 24 Farnyhurst and 40 Justice Clerk (checked after the reading)

texts.label: R4841, Add MS 32657 ff. 167-168, Wotton to Walsingham, 25 Aug 1585 (draft)
texts.summary: Gray [39] urges that while Arran [19] is in favour with the King [10] the banished lords can never be restored nor a league with England made safe, and proposes that Elizabeth fund the lords to take Arran and seize the King's person; rumours that Arran and Ferniehirst [24] are agreed and that 24 may carry the King to France.

reading_review.note: Wotton's own clear draft transcribed in full from the four DECODE images (texts/R4841_transcription.txt, struck words and interlineations marked) and read in its last state; b16_wotton_align.py: of 594 reading words/codes 581 are carried by the transcription in order or as interlineations, the other 13 are modernised spellings of words in it (towarde, continew, hable ...); supplied words bracketed. Holes: one illegible word ('with a [..] heart'); 'premoveable'/'stick' doubtful. Code 3 glossed the Queen of England from the drafts (sense, flagged).

texts.label: R4842, Add MS 32657 ff. 173-174, 30 Aug 1585 (draft)
texts.summary: Answers Walsingham's letter of the 21st about Gray's complaint; 27 and 40; Arran still at Kinneil under guard; Bothwell come to court 'to the great grief of the Arranistes'; the Jesuits Hay and Dury in the country.

reading_review.note: Wotton's own clear draft transcribed in full from the four DECODE images (texts/R4842_transcription.txt) and read in its last state; 726 of 749 reading words/codes carried by the transcription, the other 23 modernised spellings. The heavily revised passage on embarking the Scots (p2.05-p2.09) and two short interlineations are partly illegible and left [..]; codes 27 and 11 open; 'Jamington' doubtful.

texts.label: R4843, Add MS 32657 ff. 175-176, 1 Sep 1585 (draft)
texts.summary: The device of Gray and the Prior of Blantyre: the lords to join with Maxwell [20] under colour of his feud and send 500 men to seize the King and Arran, the plan that became the lords' return and Arran's fall at Stirling in November 1585.

reading_review.note: Wotton's own clear draft transcribed in full from the four DECODE images (texts/R4843_transcription.txt) and read in its last state; 642 of 663 reading words/codes carried, the other 21 modernised spellings or the expanded abbreviation Arb: (Arbroath). The commissioners passage (p2.10-p2.17) is heavily revised and read only in its legible last state; initials L. B., L. H., S. J. H., S. not expanded; codes 27, 32, 36 open.

outcome.fraction_read_source: Reading audit, 22 Oct 2026: none of the three drafts is transcribed in the repository, so no tokens are in a document that reads. Re-read 22 Oct 2026 (b16): all three drafts transcribed and read, so 2,866 of 2,866 transcription tokens (883 + 1,088 + 895, _check_profile.py --measure --drop-first) are in documents that read.

gaps.detail: No key on DECODE or in Tomokiyo; CSP Scotland viii, which glosses 19, 24, 39, 40, could not be reached on 22 Oct 2026 (HathiTrust Cloudflare check, archive.org lending-only). 27: favourer of the Hamiltons, Gray's colleague; 32: a place the King might flee to; 36: source of money for Gray's hundred men; 11: 'the 11 course'.

gaps.item: A few interlineations and struck-over phrases in R4842 p2.05-p2.09 and R4843 p2.10-p2.17
gaps.detail: Read at native resolution in zooms; the last state of the revision cannot be fixed with confidence; left [..] in the readings.
